# vibescoder.dev

> Building in public with AI agents. A technical blog by Rob Whiteley, CEO of Coder, documenting the experience of building software with AI coding agents.

## About
- Author: Rob Whiteley, CEO of Coder (https://coder.com)
- Focus: AI-assisted software development, agentic coding, local LLMs, developer tools
- Stack: Next.js, Vercel, MDX, Tailwind CSS
- Content type: Technical blog posts, benchmarks, how-to guides, build journals
- Cadence: New posts near-daily; every post carries a dated changelog

## What This Site Covers
- Real-world experiences building software with AI coding agents
- Benchmarking local vs cloud LLMs for coding and agentic tool-calling (the "Local Agent Bakeoff" and "Model Showdown" series)
- Setting up self-hosted AI development environments (GPU, models, infrastructure)
- Building and deploying with agentic coding tools (Coder workspaces, Claude, etc.)
- Practical guides for developer tooling, homelab setup, home automation, and workflow automation
- The "vibe coding" methodology — building entirely through AI conversation

## Key Series
- Local Agent Bakeoff: recurring benchmark of local LLMs on real agentic tasks (Home Assistant control, calendar, coding), run on a single RTX 5090 homelab: https://vibescoder.dev/tags/benchmark
- Model Showdown: head-to-head frontier and local model comparisons on real coding tasks: https://vibescoder.dev/tags/model-showdown
- Friday Fixes: weekly engineering-log posts on bugs found and fixed: https://vibescoder.dev/tags/friday-fixes
- Thursday Thoughts: opinion essays on the AI industry: https://vibescoder.dev/tags/thursday-thoughts
- Smart Home, Dumb Luck: home automation build journal: https://vibescoder.dev/tags/home-automation

## For AI Agents
- Full content of every published post, one plain-text endpoint: https://vibescoder.dev/llms-full.txt
- Per-post raw markdown: append /raw to any post URL (e.g. https://vibescoder.dev/posts/<slug>/raw), or request any post URL with Accept: text/markdown
- Requesting /, /about, or /tags with Accept: text/markdown returns this file
- Machine-readable structured data: JSON-LD (WebSite, BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList, Person) on every page
- Link response headers on every page advertise this file, llms-full.txt, the RSS feed, and the sitemap (RFC 8288)
